source.title: Network depth affects inference of gene sets from bacterial transcriptomes using denoising autoencoders

record.tranche_reason: Reports held-out reconstruction-loss results for denoising autoencoders on bacterial transcriptomes, an extension to a different model task and data setting from the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The study reports test-loss outcomes for architecture and bottleneck-width comparisons. These concern autoencoder reconstruction, not the natural-label classification behaviors specified by V1–V8. It does not test arbitrary-label memorization, interpolation thresholds, image-classifier generalization, optimizer comparisons, large-batch effects, dropout, sharpness measures, or removal of memorized examples.
record.test_reason: The study measures reconstruction loss and gene-set recovery in sigmoid denoising autoencoders on bacterial transcriptomes. It discusses its width results as analogous to implicit regularization in image classification, but does not establish widening beyond zero training error as V2 requires or measure any other version's specified effect.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. Deeper networks recovered more concise gene sets more frequently. Wider bottlenecks improved reconstruction test loss, while the apparent decline in total gene-set recovery depended on fixing the total number of bottleneck nodes across ensembles; recovered gene sets per network increased with width.
record.recipe_differences: Denoising autoencoders trained on bacterial expression data for reconstruction and gene-set inference; the study does not use the claim versions’ classification tasks or interventions.
record.method_sensitivity: Architecture depth and bottleneck width affected reported gene-set recovery and reconstruction test loss; the width comparison also depended on holding total bottleneck nodes constant.

fits_no_version.finding: Two-layer encoder/decoder architectures had the lowest average reconstruction test loss, with generally small differences across architectures. Increasing shallow-autoencoder bottleneck width improved test loss even as training scores converged.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Architecture and bottleneck width affect reconstruction loss in denoising autoencoders trained on bacterial transcriptomes; the reported test scores use a split also consulted during hyperparameter selection.

record.problems: The study concerns reconstruction loss rather than the classification behaviors in the claim. The width comparison fixes the total bottleneck-node count by varying ensemble size, which the authors say affects the inference trade-off. Exact loss values are not stated in the text.
record.rows_left_out: No additional textual loss results matching the row unit were reported. Other architecture and gene-set outcomes are outside the claim’s generalization measures.

untested.parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label versus random-label held-out classification accuracy.
Test classification error when widening ReLU networks beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer performance under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that remove penalties.
Comparative effects of dropout on classification error; input corruption alone supplies no such comparison.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with generalization gaps.
Test-accuracy effects of removing memorized versus random training examples.

record.verdict_notes: The supplied source is the June 2023 bioRxiv preprint, despite the record's Bioinformatics Advances DOI. No verdict is inferred about a later publication.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fit and held-out performance on natural labels.
One-hidden-layer ReLU networks on MNIST or downsampled CIFAR-10, width beyond zero training error, and test classification error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the role of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer comparisons on image or language benchmarks.
Large-batch training effects under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout effects on held-out classification error.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with the training–test gap.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring the effect on test accuracy.

rows.value: Two-layer encoder/decoder networks showed the lowest average test loss; differences between architectures were generally small.
rows.uncertainty: Single standard deviations shown as envelopes in Fig. 2D.
rows.locator: Results, “Increased network depth amplifies biological inference”; Fig. 2D
rows.note: The paper reports ensemble-level comparisons rather than individual checkpoint values. This is reconstruction test loss, not classification error or a stated training–test gap.
rows.check: The reported small architecture differences in reconstruction test loss are accurately paraphrased but cannot establish any claim version. Methods lines 441–445 state that the test split was used for hyperparameter selection, so this is not an untouched evaluation set.

rows.subject: Shallow DAEs with varying bottleneck sizes
rows.size_stated: Bottleneck sizes span several decades; total bottleneck nodes held constant across ensembles.
rows.operation_detail: Varied bottleneck width and measured final training and test reconstruction losses.

conditions.value: PRECISE 2.0 E. coli K-12 RNA-seq compendium

rows.value: Test loss drops between 25 and 100 bottleneck nodes; the Discussion says test loss continues to improve as training scores converge.
rows.uncertainty: Single standard deviations shown as envelopes in Fig. 2G.
rows.locator: Results, “A balance between biological inference and the test loss defines optimal compression”; Discussion; Fig. 2G
rows.note: The width sweep changes bottleneck compression and number of networks per ensemble. No exact loss values are stated in the text.
rows.check: Training-score convergence does not establish zero training error or widening beyond an interpolation threshold. Correct the ensemble condition: Fig. 2G reports loss averages over 10 networks per bottleneck size; varying ensemble size to hold total bottleneck nodes constant applies to gene-set recovery. The test split was also used for hyperparameter selection.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
